messages:
rowan: quick note: while walking a new hire through the go generator sample, we hit a subtle cancellation + auth retry mismatch. long-lived stream + token refresh/retry kept a goroutine alive after ctx cancel.

kevin: can you describe the parity issue?

rowan: sample app spawns a background refresh loop (old TokenSource interface) that calls a blocking refresh function. main uses context cancellation for SIGTERM. when ctx is cancelled the stream returns, but background refresh still blocks, preventing process exit.

maya: this sounds like both an SDK ergonomics and docs problem. new users expect signal cancel to tear everything down.

kevin: agree. two fixes: make sampleapp demonstrate signal.NotifyContext and use a cancellable http request for refresh; additionally the SDK should offer a context-aware adapter for legacy token sources so customers don't have to rewrite their auth code.

rowan: I'll open a small sampleapp PR to show the pattern and add a blurb in the onboarding README.

maya: please add a unit/integration test that simulates a stalled token endpoint (test server that accepts conn but delays) so CI can catch regressions.

ci-bot: Created ticket RW-4292: "go sdk: add context-aware token refresh adapter + sampleapp updates" and scheduled e2e run.

rowan: thanks. small followup: also call out this behaviour in the "generator streaming checklist" so platform teams don't copy the naive pattern into long-lived pods.
